findings.status: Bounded nonfinding and evidence refinement for open historical contracts; no new defect count
findings.first_contract: In the native source, derive dispatch selects opaque reflection and, if enabled, the opaque FromReflect generator. The ordinary generator downcasts an already typed Self and clones it; the remote generator downcasts the declared remote type, clones it, then maps to its generated wrapper. Opaque apply similarly replaces the entire downcast typed value, and mismatched types return an error without that replacement. Generated remote wrapper is repr(transparent) over the remote type and exports whole-remote references and conversions; it is not itself a validator of that remote type.
findings.current_trace: PositiveLength has private f32 backing, explicit finite strictly positive admission and checked manual Serde; reflect(opaque) is conditionally compiled behind its optional reflect feature. Current animation wrappers declare reflect_remote(AnimationElapsed) and reflect_remote(UnitInterval), not f32, and include opaque and transparent-Serde attributes. Those two remote owners have private f32 backing and try_from-based checked Serde. DirectControlState declares fields using these wrapper types as remote-reflection adapters. These are source-backed relationships; no macro expansion, reflection apply, serialization, feature resolution, network delivery or invalid-instance construction was executed.
findings.conditions_and_limits: The typed-clone route preserves whatever value was already admitted; it cannot repair an invalid value previously fabricated through some other construction or mutation route. The exact application Deserialize dispatcher and all constructors/feature activation remain open. Safe, sound construction requires the advertised remote wrapper relationship and ownership invariant; source-derived assertions above do not prove every unsafe generic or foreign wrapper case.

findings.status: Source-level conditional question; not a demonstrated supported product defect
findings.first_contract: For a struct with metadata REFLECT_DEFAULT, the generated FromReflect constructor starts from Default and only overwrites a field if extraction and conversion yield Some; missing or failing field conversion retains the default while other convertible fields may be assigned. Without this metadata, the generated construction requires each active value (or its declared field default).
findings.current_trace: PlayerInputRequest derives Reflect, Default, Serialize and Deserialize and explicitly annotates reflect(Default). It is registered as an unreliable client event; the server-side source includes a separate player-input validation function. The event registration alone does not establish that network decoding uses Reflect::FromReflect or that a partially reflected object reaches gameplay. No caller or execution demonstrating a changed command is known in these bounded reads.

Exact semantics for optional/missing fields and first failure remain policy questions; serde wire admission must not be conflated with reflection construction.

nonfindings.claim: The disabled-auto-FromReflect branch emits no automatic reconstruction; it is an explicit supported opt-out rather than evidence of a missing implementation.

Opaque whole-value reflection does not walk or directly mutate the private scalar field in the inspected ordinary and remote generation branches. This does not attest validity of all possible pre-existing values.

Generic FromReflect struct and enum routes and unsafe remote field conversion are distinct from opaque routing. Source demonstrates those branches but their helper bodies, other project owners and unsafe assumptions are not exhausted.
Native package source has token/attribute identifiers and compiler diagnostics, not evidence of a project-owned string-identity duplication.

lenses.assessment: Typed project owners flow through opaque remote wrappers into specific reflected fields; actual runtime producers and consumers remain unproved.
Reuse AnimationElapsed, UnitInterval and PositiveLength at native reflection ports rather than substitute raw f32 solely for framework access; current wrappers target typed owners.
PositiveLength and elapsed/fraction checked constructors and decoders are separate from the native typed-clone path. No universal package admission proof follows from one wrapper.

Opaque reflect clones/replaces whole typed values; defaultable struct reconstruction selectively preserves default fields on failure. Clone validity and external typed-value fabrication remain owner-specific.
Field-by-field default reconstruction can form a mixed default/reflected record; whether that violates any PlayerInputRequest relation and reaches supported consumers remains open.
Native reflective metadata and remote wrapper are adapters for owning project types, not replacement semantic validators or project Git definitions.
The wrapper retains a typed remote value rather than independently storing another f32; framework registry metadata and owner validation have distinct roles.
Maintain zero-valid elapsed, inclusive fraction bounds, strictly positive lengths, opaque whole-value semantics and explicit FromReflect opt-out; no execution attests behavior.
Native derive selects Struct, TupleStruct, Enum or Opaque branches deliberately. No isolated enum-shape repair follows from this package scope.
Generated reflection saves boilerplate when its contract matches an owner; checked Serde and opaque attributes are meaningful and cannot be removed based only on derivability.
Native framework reflection traits and typed elapsed/fraction/length domains represent distinct roles; do not erase invariant distinctions with a shared raw scalar.
Native macro attribute names, generated identifiers, feature names and compiler paths are framework grammar; no project classifier error established.
Numeric boundaries remain with checked project owners; native field indexing and a few structural constants are framework internals rather than standalone project magic-number defects.
